## Purpose

A `*Source` union answers "where did this come from" — which intervention produced a token saving, which scanner discovered a sub-spec row. It is the vocabulary the UI groups and labels by, so it is declared once as a closed literal union in the wire-type modules and reused wherever a breakdown is rendered. Both exemplars treat provenance as data worth surfacing rather than collapsing: the savings breakdown keeps one row per intervention, and the spec-child row says whether it was found in the event store, on disk, or both. The Rust spellings ride through unchanged because these values arrive over `serde`.

## Convention

Folder: apps/dashboard/src/lib/types/** · Extension: .ts · Files of this role in this subproject: 2

- Closed string-literal union with the backend's exact spelling — snake_case in `economy.ts` (`"rtk_rewrite" | "model_routing_downgrade" | "bash_guard_block" | "budget_output_cut"`), plain lowercase in `specs.ts` (`"event" | "header" | "both"`). No `enum`, no const object.
- The two exemplars differ in placement: a union reused across rows is a named `export type` (`SavingsSource`, documented as "Stable snake_case keys for `SavingsSource` (`mustard_core::economy`)"); a union used by exactly one field is written inline on that field (`SpecChild.source?`). Name it when more than one shape needs it.
- Inline provenance fields added after the shape shipped are optional (`source?`) with a comment naming the wave that introduced them and stating that older payloads never populate the field — the UI must tolerate `undefined`.
- Each variant gets a doc line explaining what it means, listed one per line when the union is inline (`"event"` — found only in the SQLite projection; `"header"` — found only via the on-disk scan; `"both"` — present in both).
- A named source union comes with its row and aggregate: `SavingsBySource { source, tokens_saved, event_count }` and `SavingsBreakdown { total_tokens_saved, per_source: SavingsBySource[] }`, with a doc naming the Rust struct they match and the component that renders them.
- These types live in the module that mirrors the owning Rust module, under the same header comment stating the lockstep obligation with the backend file.

## How to apply

Add the union to the existing `src/lib/types/<domain>.ts` that mirrors the Rust module producing it. Copy the serde spellings exactly, doc each variant, and if the breakdown is rendered as rows, add the `*BySource` row and the aggregate holding `per_source` beside it. When you are extending a shape that is already on the wire, make the field optional and say in the comment which payloads omit it, rather than making existing callers handle a new required field.

## Examples

- Ref: apps/dashboard/src/lib/types/economy.ts — `SavingsSource` with `SavingsBySource` and `SavingsBreakdown` directly below it.
- Ref: apps/dashboard/src/lib/types/specs.ts — `SpecChild.source?: "event" | "header" | "both"` documented variant by variant, optional for pre-Wave-6 payloads.
